requirements.text: The system shall provide one-point access to data from the sites in well-documented, and standardized formats.
The system shall have the capability to translate data from location-specific formats into the standardized STEWARDS formats.
The system shall consist of a central database management system for the storage and management of data, and a client application to allow users access and interact with the data.
The system shall operate with the following Web browsers: Microsoft Internet Explorer versions 5.0 and 6.0, Netscape Communicator version 4.7, Netscape versions 6 and 7, and FireFox.
The system shall operate on Certified and Accredited servers running the current corporate approved versions of operating systems as appropriate.
The system shall use the current corporate standard Microsoft SQL Server database engine.
The system shall be in compliance with all Accessibility, Web Design, and Security policies applicable.
The system shall provide web-based geographic information tools to allow site-specific data to be viewed within their spatial context.
The system shall be available to the intended audience 24 hours per day, 7 days a week with, 99% availability and a tolerance of -5%.
The system shall implement security controls in accordance with NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 moderate baseline requirements.
The system shall enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all administrative and data-uploader accounts and utilize encrypted transport (TLS 1.2 or higher) for all authentication traffic.
The system shall provide a response for data retrieval requests within 30 minutes for datasets up to 1GB, or provide a progress notification and estimated time of completion for larger requests.
The system shall maintain 99% availability during core business hours (08:00-17:00 EST, Monday-Friday), excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
The system shall implement session-aware load balancing across at least two application servers to ensure high availability and seamless failover in the event of a single server node failure.
The system shall return query results for metadata within 2 seconds for 95% of requests under a concurrent load of 50 users.
The system shall achieve a page load time of less than 3 seconds for the primary dashboard on a standard 10 Mbps connection.
The system shall provide a progress indicator for long-running data extractions and complete the retrieval of datasets up to 1GB within 30 minutes.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'confidentiality agreements' and 'sensitive data' but does not define the data classification levels or the specific access control policy for different user classes. - The system shall implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to enforce data sensitivity levels, ensuring that only authorized users can access restricted datasets as defined by the data classification policy.

OPEN: The requirement to support legacy browsers (IE 5.0/6.0, Netscape 4.7) directly conflicts with modern security standards and encryption protocols. - The system shall only support modern, actively maintained web browsers that support current TLS encryption standards (TLS 1.2+).

OPEN: The PRD acknowledges that data in transit could be lost or compromised but dismisses the need for protection, which is a security failure. - The system shall ensure the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit by enforcing end-to-end encryption using TLS 1.2 or higher for all data transfers between watershed sites and the central database.

OPEN: The storage requirement lacks specific capacity planning metrics, referring only to 'hundreds of megabytes' or 'Gigabytes' without a growth projection or retention policy. - The system shall support an initial storage capacity of 1TB with a scalable architecture capable of expanding to 10TB over a 5-year period to accommodate projected watershed data growth.

OPEN: The PRD mentions potential growth to Gigabytes of data but lacks specific capacity planning metrics for storage growth, throughput, or concurrent user scaling. - The system shall support a storage growth rate of 50GB per year and maintain performance levels with up to 200 concurrent active users.
